answer: Tie payouts to a slow-earned history instead of headcount. Each new identity starts with a weak vote and only gains weight after its answers are graded well by randomly drawn peers over many epochs. A sybil farm can mint keys as cheaply as writing a cipher, but it cannot fake a long thread of judged work; that track record becomes a relic that took real time to build, so spinning up a thousand fresh accounts buys a thousand voices nobody listens to yet.
